arguments.value: Erchonia granted InnerScope an exclusive, non-transferable right to promote, distribute, and sell certain Erchonia laser products in the licensed territory, for use only by approved licensed health care professionals and only for the treatment of hearing disorders. InnerScope must use its best efforts to market the products, meet minimum performance goals once set, keep sales records and provide reports on request, promptly report complaints or side effects, follow Erchonia’s use restrictions, act professionally, comply with all laws, and not sell competing products without Erchonia’s written consent. Erchonia may change or discontinue the products, and InnerScope must stop selling replaced or discontinued versions and return certain returned products to Erchonia, which will reimburse related costs. InnerScope must pay for products as specified, with half paid before shipment and the balance 30 days after shipment, and late payments incur a fee. The agreement lasts three years and renews for another three years if both parties agree on new minimum performance goals; either party may terminate for material breach after notice and a 10-day cure period, and Erchonia may terminate immediately if InnerScope becomes insolvent or bankrupt. The agreement also covers confidentiality, intellectual property, trademarks, limited warranties, indemnification, arbitration, and other standard terms. The source states the agreement is governed by the laws of the United States and the State of Florida, with venue and personal jurisdiction in Brevard County, Florida.
